**Slide 4**: planning steps are to familiarise yourself with the subject so you can frame insightful questions, identify the most critical information gaps, then prioritise research needs. Before launching, consider the **ethics and etiquette** of your approach.

en: Step
Activities
1 Plan
Maintain research ethics and etiquette; familiarise yourself with the subject and develop a problem statement; identify information gaps; prioritise research needs
ms: Kekalkan etika dan etiket penyelidikan; kenali subjek dan bangunkan penyataan masalah; kenal pasti jurang maklumat; utamakan keperluan penyelidikan

en: 2 Locate data and information
Evaluate sources; collect secondary information at the library, online or elsewhere; document your sources; collect primary information through surveys and interviews
ms: Nilai sumber; kumpul maklumat sekunder di perpustakaan, dalam talian atau tempat lain; dokumenkan sumber; kumpul maklumat primer melalui tinjauan dan temu bual

en: 3 Process data and information
Quote, paraphrase or summarise textual information; analyse numerical information
ms: Petik, parafrasa atau ringkaskan maklumat teks; analisis maklumat berangka

en: 4 Apply your findings
Summarise findings; draw conclusions; make recommendations
ms: Ringkaskan dapatan; buat kesimpulan; beri cadangan

en: 5 Manage information
Make research results available to others via your company’s knowledge management system
ms: Sediakan hasil penyelidikan kepada orang lain melalui sistem pengurusan pengetahuan syarikat

blocks.en: Mnemonic for Figure 13.1: Plan → Locate → Process → Apply → Manage.
blocks.ms: Cara ingat Rajah 13.1: Plan → Locate → Process → Apply → Manage.

blocks.en: Figure 13.1 (slides 4–5) is the five-step research process. The slide notes say that following a methodical process **saves time and money while uncovering better information**.
blocks.ms: Rajah 13.1 (slaid 4–5) ialah proses penyelidikan lima langkah. Nota slaid: proses teratur **menjimatkan masa dan wang serta menghasilkan maklumat lebih baik**.

blocks.en: Chapter opener (slide 1 photo): Alex Osterwalder’s Business Model Canvas, a simpler and faster alternative to the traditional business plan for evaluating new business ideas.
blocks.ms: Pembuka bab (gambar slaid 1): Business Model Canvas oleh Alex Osterwalder, pilihan lain lebih mudah dan pantas berbanding pelan perniagaan tradisional untuk menilai idea perniagaan baharu.

en: Don’t force a specific outcome — Approach research with an open mind, even if you don’t like what you find.
Respect the privacy of research participants — Businesses want to protect confidential information from competitors; consumers want to protect personal information from businesses.
Document sources and give credit — Fair to creators, and lets your audience confirm or explore the information.
Respect intellectual property rights — A great business process you find may be protected by a patent.
Don’t misquote your sources — If an expert says a sales increase is *possible*, don’t quote “*probable*”.

Don’t make misrepresentations — **Sugging** = *selling under the guise of research* (a “survey” used to find hot sales leads, or following a genuine survey with sales calls using respondents’ answers).
ms: Jangan paksa hasil tertentu — Minda terbuka walaupun dapatan tidak disukai.
Hormati privasi peserta penyelidikan — Perniagaan melindungi maklumat sulit daripada pesaing; pengguna melindungi maklumat peribadi daripada perniagaan.
Dokumenkan sumber dan beri kredit — Adil kepada pencipta dan membolehkan audiens mengesahkan.
Hormati hak harta intelek — Proses perniagaan mungkin dilindungi paten.
Jangan salah petik sumber — Jika pakar kata kenaikan jualan *mungkin*, jangan petik “*berkemungkinan besar*”.
Jangan membuat salah nyata — **Sugging** = *menjual berselindung di sebalik penyelidikan* (tinjauan untuk cari bakal pelanggan, atau panggilan jualan selepas tinjauan sebenar).

en: Explore the subject area: industry publications, websites and social media, interviews — Give yourself unstructured time to explore: industry publications and blogs, trending topics on Twitter, competitors’ websites, interviews with experts in your organisation, tables of contents and indexes of books.

Develop a problem statement: define purpose, identify conclusion, phrase the problem as a question — Defines the problem or purpose: the decision you must make or the conclusion you must reach. Easier as a question, e.g. “How can we improve customer satisfaction?” or “Does Apple’s new TV system pose a competitive threat to us?”
ms: Teroka bidang subjek: penerbitan industri, laman web dan media sosial, temu bual — Beri masa tidak berstruktur untuk meneroka: penerbitan industri, blog, topik trending Twitter, laman pesaing, temu bual pakar dalaman, kandungan dan indeks buku.

Bangunkan pernyataan masalah: tentukan tujuan, kenal pasti kesimpulan, bingkai masalah sebagai soalan — Menentukan masalah atau tujuan: keputusan atau kesimpulan yang perlu dicapai. Lebih mudah sebagai soalan.

en: Find specific information gaps — The problem statement does not say what specific information you need. You or someone in the company may already have some of it. “Improve customer satisfaction” is too vague, so break it into issues (product reliability, customer service skills). If repair data are already tracked, no need to research reliability; if service skills were never measured, that is a definite gap.
Dig deeper into purpose
Focus on specific issues
ms: Cari jurang maklumat khusus — Penyataan masalah tidak menyatakan maklumat khusus. Mungkin sebahagian sudah ada. Pecahkan topik kabur kepada isu khusus; jika data sudah dijejak, tidak perlu dikaji; yang belum diukur ialah jurang.

en: Constraints: limited time, limited money, unavailability of qualified subjects — You lack time and money to answer every question; interviews and surveys must be limited to what people will give. Divide into **“need to know”** and **“nice to know”** and drop “nice to know”. Information gap analysis shows what you truly need.
Information: limit the scope of surveys and interviews; “need to know” questions come before “nice to know” questions
ms: Kekangan: masa terhad, wang terhad, ketiadaan subjek berkelayakan — Masa dan wang terhad; tinjauan dan temu bual mesti dihadkan. Bahagikan kepada **“need to know”** dan **“nice to know”** dan buang “nice to know”.
Maklumat: hadkan skop tinjauan dan temu bual; soalan “need to know” sebelum “nice to know”

blocks.en: Your research tactics affect the people you gather data from and the people who read and apply your results.
blocks.ms: Taktik penyelidikan anda memberi kesan kepada orang yang memberi data dan orang yang menggunakan hasilnya.

blocks.en: **Secondary research** = consulting research done previously for another purpose (periodicals, online databases, books, research reports; some firms specialise in reports on industries, companies, technologies or regions). Start here because it can **save considerable time and money**, although you may have to pay. **Primary research** is new research done specifically for the current project.
blocks.ms: **Penyelidikan sekunder** = merujuk kajian terdahulu untuk tujuan lain. Mulakan di sini kerana **menjimatkan masa dan wang**, walaupun mungkin berbayar. **Penyelidikan primer** ialah kajian baharu khusus untuk projek semasa.

en: Reputation for honesty and reliability? — Even the finest reporters err; for new or unknown sources, **corroborate** with several other sources.
Potentially biased? — Not inherently bad or unethical *unless intentionally hidden*, but you must be aware of it.
Purpose of the material? — Distinguish **advertising, advocating and informing**.
Is the author credible? — Known and respected, with hands-on experience or merely an observer with an opinion?
Where did the source get the information? — Many secondary sources take material from other secondary sources, distancing you from the original data.
Can you verify independently? — Important for projections, interpretations and estimates; if you can’t verify critical information, tell your audience.
Is the material current? — Check publication or posting date. **Complete**: entire document or only a selection?
Is it complete?
Are all claims supported with evidence? — Are opinions presented as facts? Broad claims like “most people believe…” with no survey?
Do claims stand up to logical scrutiny? — If a little voice says it sounds suspicious, listen. Focus checks on the most important or most suspicious information.
ms: Nama baik kejujuran dan kebolehpercayaan? — Pelapor terbaik pun boleh silap; sumber baharu perlu **disahkan** dengan beberapa sumber lain.
Mungkin berat sebelah? — Tidak semestinya buruk atau tidak beretika *kecuali sengaja disembunyikan*.
Tujuan bahan? — Bezakan **pengiklanan, advokasi dan pemberitahuan**.
Adakah penulis berwibawa? — Dikenali, pengalaman sebenar atau sekadar pemerhati.
Dari mana sumber dapat maklumat? — Banyak sumber sekunder mengambil daripada sumber sekunder lain.
Boleh disahkan secara bebas? — Penting untuk unjuran, tafsiran dan anggaran; jika tidak boleh, beritahu audiens.
Adakah terkini? — Semak tarikh. **Lengkap**: dokumen penuh atau sebahagian?
Adakah semua dakwaan disokong bukti? — Adakah pendapat dibentangkan sebagai fakta?
Adakah dakwaan tahan ujian logik? — Jika terasa mencurigakan, dengar. Fokus pada maklumat paling penting atau mencurigakan.

en: Internal: documents, knowledge management system, research repository — Even if you plan primary research, **start with secondary**. Inside the company: documents from other projects and the **knowledge management system** / repository.
External: print and online resources, reference librarian, public reports — Print and online resources (Table 13.1, slide 15 is a table image) and a **reference librarian**.
ms: Dalam: dokumen, sistem pengurusan pengetahuan, repositori penyelidikan — Walaupun merancang kajian primer, **mulakan dengan sekunder**. Dalam syarikat: dokumen projek lain dan **sistem pengurusan pengetahuan**.
Luar: sumber cetak dan dalam talian, pustakawan rujukan, laporan awam — Sumber cetak dan dalam talian (Jadual 13.1, slaid 15 imej jadual) dan **pustakawan rujukan**.

en: Newspapers and periodicals — Popular and general business magazines, **trade journals** (specific professions and industries) and **academic journals** (research-oriented).

Business books — Less timely but in-depth. **Directories**: membership information. **Almanacs**: factual and statistical (e.g. *Statistical Abstract of the United States*). **Government publications**: laws, court decisions, tax and regulatory issues. **Databases**: searchable collections, some by institutional subscription only.
Directories
Almanacs and statistical resources
Government publications
Databases
ms: Akhbar dan berkala — Majalah popular, majalah perniagaan am, **jurnal perdagangan** dan **jurnal akademik**.

Buku perniagaan — Kurang terkini tetapi mendalam. **Direktori**: maklumat keahlian. **Almanak**: fakta dan statistik. **Penerbitan kerajaan**: undang-undang, keputusan mahkamah, cukai. **Pangkalan data**: ada yang perlu langganan institusi.

en: Approaches: active search tools and monitoring selected sources — **actively search** for existing information, and **monitor** selected sources for new information.
ms: Pendekatan: alat carian aktif dan memantau sumber terpilih — **mencari secara aktif** dan **memantau** sumber terpilih.

en: General-purpose search tools: pros
Cons
Ranked by usefulness; millions of webpages; powerful ranking algorithms
No human editors; no uniform search techniques; can’t reach the deep web
ms: Disusun mengikut kegunaan; jutaan halaman; algoritma kuat
Tiada penyunting manusia; teknik carian tidak seragam; tidak boleh capai deep web

en: Improved tools: web directories (human editors), metasearch engines (multiple engines, compare results), online databases (free public access), specialised search engines (focus on a media type) — **web directories** (e.g. DMOZ) use human editors, some focus on blogs or podcasts; **metasearch engines** send your request to multiple engines to compare results; **online databases** (free or subscription) reach newspapers, magazines, journals and digital books, plus specialised search engines.

Monitoring: subscribe to news feeds, follow people on Twitter, create alerts, use specialised monitors — Subscribe to newsfeeds, follow people on Twitter/microblogs, set alerts on engines and databases, use **TweetDeck** and **HootSuite**. Be careful: it is easy to be overwhelmed by information.
ms: Alat lebih baik: direktori web (penyunting manusia), enjin metacarian (banyak enjin, bandingkan), pangkalan data dalam talian (akses awam percuma), enjin carian khusus (satu jenis media) — **direktori web** guna editor manusia; **enjin metasearch** hantar carian ke banyak enjin; **pangkalan data dalam talian** capai akhbar, jurnal, buku digital serta enjin carian khusus.

Pemantauan: langgan suapan berita, ikut orang di Twitter, cipta amaran, guna pemantau khusus — Langgan newsfeed, ikut orang di Twitter, tetapkan alert, guna **TweetDeck** dan **HootSuite**. Berhati-hati dengan banjir maklumat.

en: Think before you search — Neat results create the illusion that the Internet is an orderly warehouse of all information; the reality is far different.
Pay attention to details
Don’t limit search engines
Review search and display options — Title, author, subject, full-text only, etc.

Try variations of terms — Abbreviations (CEO, CPA), synonyms, related terms, different spellings (dialog/dialogue), singular/plural, noun/adjective forms, open/compound forms (online, on line, on-line).
Adjust the scope — Too few results → use *fewer* terms to broaden; too many hits → use *more* terms to narrow.
Look beyond the first few pages — ; consider enterprise search engines, research managers like LiveBinders and Zotero, and search functions in workplace messaging and groupware.
ms: Fikir sebelum cari — Hasil kemas mencipta tipu daya Internet gudang teratur.
Semak pilihan carian dan paparan — **Semak pilihan carian dan paparan**.
Cuba kepelbagaian istilah — Singkatan, sinonim, istilah berkaitan, ejaan berbeza, tunggal/jamak, kata nama/adjektif, bentuk terbuka/majmuk.
Laraskan skop — Terlalu sedikit → kurangkan istilah; terlalu banyak → tambah istilah.
Lihat melepasi beberapa halaman pertama — ; pertimbangkan enjin carian enterprise, LiveBinders, Zotero.

en: Properly credits the originator
Shows sufficient support for your message
Helps readers explore the topic in more detail
ms: Memberi kredit sewajarnya kepada pencipta asal
Membantu pembaca meneroka topik lebih lanjut

blocks.en: You cannot assume information is accurate, objective and current. Evaluate to avoid embarrassing and damaging mistakes.
blocks.ms: Jangan andaikan maklumat tepat, objektif dan terkini.

en: **Public** companies (sell shares to the public) must file extensive financial reports, so usually have more information than **private** companies.
ms: Syarikat **awam** perlu hantar laporan kewangan terperinci, jadi biasanya lebih banyak maklumat berbanding syarikat **swasta**.

en: General-purpose engines (Google, Bing) scan millions of pages and rank by relevance. **Three shortcomings**: (1) no human editors evaluate quality or ranking; (2) engines use different techniques so results differ; (3) they can’t reach all content (the **hidden Internet / deep web**).
ms: Enjin am mengimbas berjuta laman dan meranking. **Tiga kelemahan**: (1) tiada editor manusia; (2) teknik berbeza; (3) tidak sampai semua kandungan (**hidden Internet / deep web**).

en: Use documentation tools: word processors track endnotes; citation/reference managers; footnotes or endnotes (Appendix B).

Document books, articles, tables, charts, diagrams, lyrics, dialogue, letters, speeches and anything taken, including ideas **re-expressed by paraphrasing or summarising**. **No citation** needed for general knowledge or specialised knowledge generally known to your readers.

**Copyright** covers the *expression* of ideas and starts the moment it is put into fixed form. It does **not** protect titles, names, short phrases, slogans, familiar symbols, or lists of ingredients; nor ideas, procedures, methods, systems, processes, concepts, principles, discoveries or devices (though it covers their description). Other protections apply: **trademarks** for slogans, **patents** for devices and processes.
**Fair use**: crediting the source is not always enough; you may use others’ work only if you don’t unfairly prevent them from benefiting (e.g. reproducing material they could sell to your readers).
ms: Guna alat dokumentasi: nota hujung automatik, pengurus rujukan, nota kaki atau nota hujung.
Dokumenkan semua yang diambil, termasuk idea yang **diparafrasa atau diringkas**. **Tidak perlu** untuk pengetahuan umum.

**Hak cipta** melindungi *ungkapan* idea sebaik ia dalam bentuk tetap. **Tidak** melindungi tajuk, nama, frasa pendek, slogan, simbol, senarai ramuan; atau idea, tatacara, kaedah, sistem, proses. Perlindungan lain: **tanda dagangan**, **paten**.
**Penggunaan saksama (fair use)**: memberi kredit tidak selalu cukup; jangan halang pemilik daripada mendapat manfaat.

title.ms: Penyelidikan Primer: Tinjauan dan Temu Bual

en: Must be reliable
Must be valid
Choose participants carefully
Use a research handbook or hire a research specialist
Provide clear instructions
Ask for information people can remember
Keep the questionnaire short
Formulate questions that are easy to analyse
Avoid leading questions
Avoid ambiguous descriptors
ms: Guna buku panduan penyelidikan atau upah pakar
Tanya maklumat yang orang boleh ingat

en: Question types
Interview types
Answers are influenced by the question types
Focus group

**Primary research** = collecting data and information **for the first time** rather than reusing what others found. Choose it when secondary research can’t give you what you need. Most common: **surveys and interviews**. Others: **observation** and **experiments** (e.g. test-marketing a new product).
**Online surveys**: fast, cheap, and adaptable, but vulnerable to sampling bias because only people who visit the site and want to participate respond.
ms: **Penyelidikan primer** = mengumpul data **buat kali pertama**. Pilih apabila sekunder tidak mencukupi. Paling biasa: **tinjauan dan temu bual**. Lain: **pemerhatian** dan **eksperimen**.
**Tinjauan dalam talian**: pantas, murah, boleh disesuaikan, tetapi terdedah kepada bias persampelan.

en: Must be **reliable**: produces identical results when repeated — A survey is **reliable** if it gives identical results when repeated and **valid** if it measures what it is meant to measure. Choose participants carefully; for strategic, high-stakes surveys hire a **research specialist**.
Must be **valid**: measures what it is intended to measure

Choose participants carefully: get a representative sample of the population — Is the most critical task. Surveying a few hundred people in a shopping mall is not enough: different consumers shop at different times and many rarely visit malls. A non-representative sample causes **sampling bias**.
Use a research handbook or hire a research specialist
ms: Mesti **boleh dipercayai (reliable)**: hasil sama bila diulang — Tinjauan **boleh dipercayai (reliable)** jika hasil sama bila diulang dan **sah (valid)** jika mengukur apa yang sepatutnya. Untuk tinjauan penting, upah **pakar penyelidikan**.
Mesti **sah (valid)**: mengukur apa yang sepatutnya diukur
Pilih peserta dengan teliti: sampel mewakili populasi — Ialah tugas paling penting. Tinjauan di pusat beli-belah tidak cukup. Sampel tidak mewakili menyebabkan **bias persampelan**.
Guna buku panduan penyelidikan atau upah pakar

en: Provide clear instructions — Clear instructions; don’t ask what people can’t remember (e.g. how many times they shopped for groceries last year); keep it short (**no more than 10 or 15 minutes**); prefer numbers and facts, which are easier to summarise than opinions.
Ask for information people can remember
Keep the questionnaire short
Formulate questions that are easy to analyse
Avoid leading questions — “Do you prefer that we stay open in the evenings for customer convenience?” gets a “yes”. Ask “What time of day do you normally shop?”
Avoid ambiguous descriptors — (often, frequently) mean different things to different people. **Compound questions** (“Do you read books and magazines?”) confuse respondents who read only one.
Avoid compound questions
Make the survey adaptive — Online surveys can branch based on answers, giving better answers and less frustration. **Pre-test on a sample group** to find confusing questions.
ms: Beri arahan jelas — Arahan jelas; jangan tanya perkara sukar diingat; ringkas (**tidak lebih 10 atau 15 minit**); utamakan nombor dan fakta.
Tanya maklumat yang orang boleh ingat
Elak soalan mengarah — “Adakah anda mahu kami buka petang untuk kemudahan pelanggan?” pasti dijawab “ya”.
Elak penerang kabur — (selalu, kerap) bermakna berbeza. **Soalan majmuk** mengelirukan.
Jadikan tinjauan boleh berubah ikut jawapan — Boleh bercabang ikut jawapan. **Uji dahulu pada kumpulan sampel**.

en: Question types: open-ended, closed; plan question sequence — Solicit opinions, insights and information (“Why do you believe South America is a better opportunity than Europe?”). **Closed questions** elicit a specific answer such as yes/no; too many make it feel like a survey — Plan **question sequence** to uncover layers; consider giving questions a day or two before, especially if you want to quote the subject or answers need research.

Interview types: recorded, face-to-face, group — Ask beforehand and respect wishes. During: pursue new topics that shed light. After: write down thoughts, find themes, facts and quotes; **transcribe** if recorded — Lets you gauge reactions and see nonverbal signals. **Email interviews** give time to think and may be the only way to reach some experts.
ms: Jenis soalan: terbuka, tertutup; rancang urutan soalan — Menggalak pendapat dan pandangan. **Soalan tertutup** meminta jawapan khusus; terlalu banyak menjadikan ia seperti tinjauan — Rancang **urutan soalan**; pertimbangkan beri soalan sehari dua awal.

Jenis temu bual: dirakam, bersemuka, kumpulan — Minta izin dahulu. Selepas: catat, cari tema, fakta, petikan; **salinan teks** — Membolehkan nilai reaksi dan isyarat bukan lisan. **Temu bual e-mel** memberi masa berfikir.

en: Start with the information gaps and break them into specific questions; pick an appropriate question type for each (Figure 13.2).
ms: Mulakan dengan jurang maklumat dan pecahkan kepada soalan khusus (Rajah 13.2).

en: Answers are influenced by the question types, how you ask, and the subject’s cultural and language background (race, gender, age, education, social status).

**Focus group**: a moderator guides a group while the research team observes through a **one-way mirror**; the key advantage is **group dynamics** as participants bounce ideas off each other, giving richer information than individual interviews.
ms: Jawapan dipengaruhi jenis soalan, cara bertanya dan latar budaya serta bahasa subjek.
**Kumpulan fokus**: moderator memandu kumpulan sementara pasukan memerhati melalui **cermin sehala**; kelebihan utama ialah **dinamik kumpulan**.

blocks.en: After collecting secondary and primary information, **transform** it into the content you need. Simple projects may insert material directly; with significant raw data you must process it: quoting, paraphrasing or summarising text; analysing numeric data; drawing conclusions; making recommendations.
blocks.ms: Selepas mengumpul maklumat, **ubah** kepada kandungan diperlukan. Data banyak perlu diproses: petik, parafrasa, ringkas teks; analisis data berangka; kesimpulan; cadangan.

en: Technique
Meaning
Quoting
Reproduce the material exactly
Paraphrasing
Restating it in your own words
Summarising
Similar to paraphrasing; presents the gist in fewer words
ms: Serupa parafrasa; bentang intipati dengan lebih sedikit perkataan

en: Trends — = definite patterns over time: growth, decline, and cyclical trends.
Causation
Correlation
Cross-tabulation — Explores relationships between subsets, e.g. sales by customer age and gender, location and product type.
ms: Trend — = corak jelas dari masa ke masa: pertumbuhan, penurunan, kitaran.
Jadual silang — Meneroka hubungan antara subset, cth jualan mengikut umur, jantina, lokasi, produk.

en: Guard against computational errors — Wrong formulas, references to unintended cells, unverified built-in functions; double-check and document shared spreadsheets. Step back: do numbers make sense? (A jump of 50% when it never varied more than 10% is suspicious.)
Be cautious of misrepresenting results
Avoid faulty comparisons
Don’t push results beyond their limits
Avoid misleading presentations
ms: Elak kesilapan pengiraan — Formula salah, rujukan sel tidak dimaksudkan; semak dua kali. Adakah nombor logik?

en: **Quoting** = reproducing exactly, with full credit.

**Paraphrasing** = restating in your own words and sentence structure. Benefits: consistent tone, vocabulary familiar to audience, avoids the choppy feel of too many quotations. Still credit the source.

**Five paraphrasing tips**: read and reread the passage; restate central ideas in your own words; check against the source that the meaning is unchanged; use quotation marks for unique terms borrowed exactly; record the source accurately.
**Summarising** = the gist in fewer words: main ideas and major support points, leaving out minor details and examples. Needs complete documentation too.
Preserve the intended message; double-check you didn’t subconsciously **skew** the writer’s message to fit your own needs.
ms: **Parafrasa** = menyatakan semula dengan perkataan dan struktur ayat sendiri. Manfaat: nada konsisten, perkataan biasa, tidak berpecah-pecah. Tetap beri kredit.
**Lima tip parafrasa**: baca berulang; nyatakan semula idea utama; semak makna tidak berubah; guna tanda petikan untuk istilah unik; rekod sumber.
**Meringkas** = intisari dalam kurang perkataan; perlu dokumentasi lengkap.
Kekalkan mesej asal; pastikan tidak **memesongkan** mesej untuk keperluan sendiri.

en: Numeric data (sales, population, survey answers) need processing to give insights. Simple arithmetic is powerful (Table 13.2; slide 30 is a figure).

**Mean** = sum of items ÷ number of items (the “average”). **Median** = midpoint of a series, with an equal number of items above and below. **Mode** = the number that occurs most often; best answer to “What is the usual amount?”

Measures and trends show *what* is happening; **causation** (one factor causes the other) and **correlation** (two variables change together, e.g. satisfaction falls when reliability falls) help explain *why*. Causation is easy to assume but hard to prove: you must isolate the suspected cause as the only possible source.

**Precautions**: avoid faulty comparisons (“apples to apples”); don’t push results beyond their limits (have a trusted colleague check your conclusions); avoid misleading presentations such as distorted graphs.
ms: Data berangka perlu diproses. Aritmetik mudah pun berkesan (Jadual 13.2; slaid 30 ialah rajah).
**Min** = jumlah ÷ bilangan (purata). **Median** = titik tengah siri. **Mod** = nombor paling kerap; jawapan terbaik untuk “jumlah biasa”.
Ukuran dan trend menunjukkan *apa*; **kausaliti** dan **hubung kait** membantu menerangkan *kenapa*. Kausaliti mudah diandaikan tetapi sukar dibuktikan.
**Langkah berjaga-jaga**: elak perbandingan salah; jangan lampaui had keputusan; elak persembahan mengelirukan seperti graf diputarbelit.

**Slide 33**: applying findings involves summarising results, drawing conclusions and making recommendations.

A **research summary** is an *unbiased condensation* of the entire research project (not just secondary sources). It has **no opinions, conclusions or recommendations**. Identify the main idea and key support points; separate them from details and examples (Figure 13.3); focus on the audience. A good summary may be nothing but **bad news** if that is what you found; managers respect honest, complete information.

A **conclusion** is a logical interpretation of the facts. Two criteria: (1) based **strictly on the information in your report**: no new information, and you can’t ignore information that doesn’t support it; (2) **logical**: follows inductive or deductive reasoning. Unproven premises, emotional appeals and hasty generalisations are invalid.

Personal or organisational values may influence conclusions; be aware and **explain the bias** to your audience. Team members may reach different conclusions, which is why you involve more people. Business decisions need assumptions, judgment calls and creative thinking.

A conclusion **interprets**; a **recommendation suggests what to do**. Recommendations must rest on logical analysis and sound conclusions, be **practical and acceptable** to readers, and describe the **next steps**.
ms: **Slaid 33**: menggunakan dapatan melibatkan ringkasan, kesimpulan dan cadangan.

**Ringkasan penyelidikan** ialah *pemadatan tidak berat sebelah* seluruh projek. **Tiada pendapat, kesimpulan atau cadangan**. Kenal pasti idea utama dan sokongan; fokus kepada audiens. Ringkasan boleh hanya **berita buruk** jika itu dapatan.

**Kesimpulan** ialah tafsiran logik fakta. Dua kriteria: (1) **berdasarkan maklumat dalam laporan sahaja**: tiada maklumat baharu; (2) **logik**: ikut penaakulan dari khusus ke umum atau dari umum ke khusus.
Nilai peribadi atau organisasi boleh mempengaruhi; **jelaskan bias** kepada audiens. Keputusan perniagaan memerlukan andaian, pertimbangan dan pemikiran kreatif.
Kesimpulan **mentafsir**; **cadangan menyatakan apa yang perlu dibuat**. Mesti berasaskan analisis logik, **mudah dilaksanakan dan boleh diterima**, dan menerangkan **langkah seterusnya**.

q.en: Scenario: Hana, a junior analyst, is asked whether her company should open a new branch in Johor Bahru. She types a few keywords into a search engine and uses the first blog posts she finds. She surveys 80 people at one shopping mall using questions such as “Don’t you agree our brand is the best?” and “Do you shop often and online?”. She copies a paragraph from a consultancy report without citing it, and calls some respondents later to offer a loyalty card. Her report summary says “We must open the branch” and adds a new competitor figure in the conclusion. ANALYSE the weaknesses in Hana’s research process and give your OPINION on how she should improve it (use Chapter 13).
q.ms: Senario: Hana, penganalisis junior, diminta menilai sama ada syarikat patut membuka cawangan baharu di Johor Bahru. Dia taip beberapa kata kunci dan guna blog pertama yang ditemui. Dia tinjau 80 orang di sebuah pusat beli-belah dengan soalan seperti “Bukankah jenama kami terbaik?” dan “Adakah anda kerap membeli-belah dan dalam talian?”. Dia salin satu perenggan laporan perunding tanpa rujukan, dan menelefon responden kemudian untuk menawarkan kad kesetiaan. Ringkasan laporannya berbunyi “Kita mesti buka cawangan” dan menambah angka pesaing baharu dalam kesimpulan. ANALISIS kelemahan proses penyelidikan Hana dan beri PENDAPAT bagaimana memperbaikinya (guna Bab 13).

en: Planning gaps: no problem statement or information gap analysis, no need-to-know prioritisation; follow the five-step process (3)
Weak secondary research: first search results only; evaluate sources (bias, purpose, author, currency, evidence), corroborate; use library, databases, metasearch, deep web (4)
Survey flaws: one-mall sample causes sampling bias; leading question; compound and ambiguous question; no pre-test; consider reliability and validity (5)
Ethics and law: uncited copied paragraph (documentation, copyright, fair use); sugging by calling respondents to sell; respect privacy (4)
Reporting flaws: summary includes opinion; conclusion introduces new information; conclusions must be logical and based on the report; recommendation must be practical with next steps (4)
Processing: paraphrase/quote with credit, check numbers, avoid faulty comparisons (2)
Clear OPINION with justified priorities and cause-effect reasoning (3)
ms: Kelemahan perancangan: tiada penyataan masalah atau analisis jurang maklumat, tiada keutamaan need-to-know; ikut proses lima langkah (3)
Penyelidikan sekunder lemah: hasil carian pertama sahaja; nilai sumber (bias, tujuan, penulis, kini, bukti), sahkan; guna perpustakaan, pangkalan data, metasearch, deep web (4)
Kecacatan tinjauan: sampel satu pusat beli-belah menyebabkan bias persampelan; soalan mengarah; soalan majmuk dan kabur; tiada ujian awal; pertimbang reliability dan validity (5)
Etika dan undang-undang: perenggan disalin tanpa rujukan (dokumentasi, hak cipta, fair use); sugging; hormati privasi (4)
Kecacatan laporan: ringkasan ada pendapat; kesimpulan memasukkan maklumat baharu; kesimpulan mesti logik; cadangan mudah dilaksanakan dengan langkah seterusnya (4)
Pemprosesan: parafrasa/petik dengan kredit, semak nombor, elak perbandingan salah (2)
PENDAPAT jelas dengan keutamaan, alasan dan sebab-akibat (3)

q.en: Analyse the strengths and weaknesses of general-purpose search engines for business research, and give your opinion on the best combination of tools to use.
q.ms: Analisis kekuatan dan kelemahan enjin carian am untuk penyelidikan perniagaan, dan beri pendapat tentang kombinasi alat terbaik.

en: Strengths: millions of pages scanned, ranked by usefulness with powerful algorithms (2)
Weaknesses: no human editors, different techniques, can’t reach the deep web (3)
Improvements: web directories, metasearch engines, online databases and specialised search engines (3)
Opinion with justified combination, including monitoring tools and evaluating sources (2)
ms: Kekuatan: berjuta laman diimbas, dirank dengan algoritma berkuasa (2)
Kelemahan: tiada editor manusia, teknik berbeza, tidak sampai deep web (3)
Penambahbaikan: direktori web, enjin metasearch, pangkalan data dan enjin khusus (3)
Pendapat dengan kombinasi beralasan, termasuk alat pemantauan dan penilaian sumber (2)
